source.title: Efficient Scaling of Diffusion Transformers for Text-to-Image Generation
source.authors: Hao Li; Shamit Lal; Zhiheng Li; Yusheng Xie; Ying Wang; Yang Zou; Orchid Majumder; R. Manmatha; Zhuo-Wen Tu; Stefano Ermon; Stefano Soatto; Ashwin Swaminathan

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports image-generation scaling experiments, but it does not test held-out language-model loss laws, fit power laws, assess large-run loss extrapolation, or determine compute-optimal parameter/token allocations.
record.gate_note: The study compares diffusion-model size, architecture, dataset size and caption types using TIFA, ImageReward and other image-generation metrics. Those findings are relevant to image-model scaling but do not measure the power-law loss or other outcomes named by the claim versions. It also cites Kaplan et al. as background; cited results are not recorded as study results.
record.test_reason: The study trains text-to-image diffusion transformers (0.3B–8B) and reports only TIFA, ImageReward and FID curves against training steps. It reports no held-out loss, fits no power laws, makes no extrapolations and does no compute-optimal allocation. Kaplan et al. is cited once in the introduction as background. The image-model scaling results measure a different construct from any version, so they are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that self-attention U-ViT scales more effectively than cross-attention DiT variants on TIFA/ImageReward, and that a 2.3B U-ViT beats SDXL U-Net in their controlled setting. They also conclude that larger datasets and captions with higher information density improve text-image alignment and learning efficiency.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains diffusion transformers for text-to-image generation and measures image-generation metrics; it does not use the language-model pretraining loss measurement or compute-allocation procedure in the cited scaling-law sources.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with architecture, model size, training data size and caption type. The text reports that larger LargeDiT sizes can plateau and that further enlargement of the 2.3B U-ViT did not significantly improve performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Image-generation metrics plateau with model size: the 7.6B LargeDiT is similar to the 4.4B, and the 3.1B/3.7B U-ViT are no significant improvement over the 2.3B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For text-to-image DiTs at 256px and fixed steps, gains in TIFA/ImageReward from model size can saturate in the 2–8B range.

fits_no_version.finding: Scaling data from 250M to 600M image-text pairs improves TIFA/ImageReward across architectures, and U-ViT gains more than SDXL.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In text-to-image diffusion, more training data improves alignment metrics, with architecture-dependent gains.

fits_no_version.finding: Long synthetic captions improve TIFA over original captions for a 0.6B U-ViT; the authors attribute this to information density.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Caption information density affects text-image alignment in diffusion training.

fits_no_version.finding: A self-attention U-ViT reaches SDXL-level TIFA at 2.3B, while cross-attention PixArt-α at 3B stays below SD2 U-Net.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Architecture family strongly changes how alignment metrics scale with size for text-to-image DiTs.

record.problems: The relevant results use image-generation metrics rather than held-out loss; several scale comparisons are stated qualitatively or presented in plots, and the text reports no uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: Additional model curves, image metrics, architecture comparisons and ablations appear in Figures 3–8 and 15–18 and Tables 1–5. They were not included because they do not measure any version of the claim; selected explicit scaling and data/caption outcomes are retained as findings outside the claim versions.

untested.parts: No held-out pretraining loss and no power-law fit in parameters, tokens or compute; only image-generation metrics.
No fits on small runs and no prediction of larger runs.
No fixed-compute sweep and no optimal parameter/data split.
Depth and width are varied, but not at a fixed parameter count, and not on loss. The architecture-family comparisons (Fig. 6) use TIFA.
Image diffusion models are scaled, but no loss is reported and no power-law form is fitted or tested.
TIFA/ImageReward are tracked against size, but there is no predictive relation with scale or loss for language models, and no fitted trend.
No fitted exponents or allocations to compare across setups.

record.verdict_notes: This is an image-generation study with no loss measurements; its only link to the claim is a background citation of Kaplan et al. Results are read from training-step curves without uncertainty estimates. The models are trained to a fixed number of steps rather than to convergence or compute-matched budgets, so the size comparisons confound size with undertraining.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out language-model loss versus parameters, tokens or compute; no power-law fits.
No small-run loss fits or predictions of larger-run loss.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or loss-minimising parameter/token split.
No test of how architecture details affect language-model loss.
The study scales image-generation models and datasets, but does not test whether the same power-law form holds for loss in image or other modalities, or in other training regimes.
No downstream language-task performance or relationship between downstream performance and pretraining loss.
No fitted exponents, compute-optimal allocations, or analysis of dependence on fitting choices or power-law curve bending.

rows.subject: PixArt-α variants (0.48B–3.0B; individual variants listed in Fig. 3)
rows.operation_detail: Scaled depth and width and evaluated TIFA during training.

conditions.value: SD2 U-Net trained for the same steps

rows.baseline: SD2 U-Net reaches 0.80 TIFA at 250K steps.
rows.value: The 0.9B PixArt-α variant gets 0.78 at 250K steps; the 3B PixArt-α model still cannot match SD2 U-Net within the same training steps.
rows.note: The paper gives explicit text results for the 0.9B and 3B variants; other curve values are figure-only.
rows.check: This row compares PixArt-α variants with an SD2 U-Net baseline across architectures. It is not a scaling effect on loss, so 'partial' has no version to be read against.

rows.subject: LargeDiT-h1536-d42-n32
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated the scaled LargeDiT model during training.
rows.baseline: SD2 U-Net reaches 0.80 TIFA; the comparison is shown in Figure 4.
rows.value: 0.80 TIFA; described as on par with SD2 U-Net.
rows.note: This is image-generation alignment, not held-out language-model loss.
rows.check: This row compares a single LargeDiT size with SD2 U-Net. It is an architecture comparison, not a scaling trend, so 'observed' has no version referent.

rows.subject: LargeDiT variants (2.9B–7.6B; individual variants listed in Figure 4)
rows.operation_detail: Scaled model size and evaluated TIFA during training.
rows.baseline: SD2 U-Net and SDXL U-Net comparisons shown in Figure 4.
rows.value: LargeDiT begins to surpass SD2 U-Net at 2.9B; 4.4B variants are close to SDXL TD4-4 U-Net at 600K steps; the 7.6B variant is similar to the 4.4B version, with a remaining gap to SDXL U-Net.
rows.note: The text reports a plateau at the largest size rather than a fitted scaling curve.

rows.subject: U-ViT-h2048-d42-n16
rows.operation_detail: Scaled hidden dimension and evaluated TIFA and ImageReward.
rows.baseline: SD2 U-Net and SDXL U-Net are the stated comparison models; exact values not stated in text.
rows.value: Significantly better performance than SD2 U-Net and matches SDXL U-Net in both TIFA and ImageReward after 500K steps.
rows.note: The stated outcomes are image-generation metrics.
rows.check: This row compares a single U-ViT size with SD2/SDXL U-Nets, using values read from figures. It is an architecture comparison, not a scaling measure for any version.

rows.subject: U-ViT-h2048-d56-n16
rows.operation_detail: Increased depth on top of the 2.3B U-ViT configuration and evaluated performance.
rows.baseline: 2.3B U-ViT; exact values not stated in text.
rows.value: No significantly improved performance was observed from further increasing the model.
rows.note: The text reports the qualitative comparison, without numerical values.

rows.subject: U-ViT-h2560-d42-n16
rows.operation_detail: Increased hidden dimension on top of the 2.3B U-ViT configuration and evaluated performance.
rows.baseline: 2.3B U-ViT; exact values not stated in text.
rows.value: No significantly improved performance was observed from further increasing the model.
rows.note: The text reports the qualitative comparison, without numerical values.

rows.subject: U-ViT-h2048-d42-n16
rows.operation_detail: Increased training data from LensArt to LensArt plus SSTK.
rows.baseline: Same model trained on LensArt alone; exact metric values not stated in text.
rows.value: The larger dataset improves performance; U-ViT surpasses SDXL at 150K steps with the larger dataset, whereas it does not match SDXL on LensArt alone until 400K or 500K steps.
rows.note: The result concerns image-generation metrics and dataset scaling, not a loss power law.

rows.subject: U-ViT-h1152-d28-n16
rows.operation_detail: Trained with original captions, a 50/50 mixture of original and long synthetic captions, or SSTK captions.
rows.baseline: LensArt with original captions; exact values not stated in text.
rows.value: LensArt augmented with long captions performs better than LensArt with original captions and SSTK.
rows.note: The finding is about image-text alignment under caption changes.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
